clue.text: Entertaining pair open country clubs, shrouded by uncertainty

indicators.note: something shrouded by another thing is wrapped up inside it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: uncertainty means doubt
a lea is a poetic word for open grassland or meadow
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A pair of entertainers keep turning up at rural country clubs amid general uncertainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Two performers who work together as a comic team, like Morecambe and Wise, are an entertaining pair.

clue.text: Initially prefers interpretive dance over salsa, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the picked letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top
initially means take the opening letter of each of the next few words

explanation.surface: Someone prefers interpretive dance to salsa, the Latin dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Salsa looks like the dance after 'interpretive dance', but here it is the tomato sauce, defined by example ('say').
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy sauce served for scooping tortilla chips into, so it is an example of a dip.

clue.text: Single elements burn pittas every so often

indicators.note: every so often means take letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: An instruction-manual warning: these individual heating elements will burn pitta breads now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Single elements of a whole are its individual components, the separate ones that make it up.

clue.text: End holidays elsewhere

parts.note: holidays from work are leave, as in annual leave
off means away, somewhere else, as in 'she is off today'

explanation.surface: The phrase sounds like the end of the holidays, or holidaying abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or stop doing something is to quit it, as in 'please stop that teasing'.

clue.text: Australian half of 1A visits mother country; …

indicators.note: to visit is to go in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Eric Morecambe was one half of the comic double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: An Australian member of a comedy pair goes home to see Mum in the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is double acts; ERIC is Eric Morecambe of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States of America is a nation, commonly called by this shortened name.

clue.text: … their little partner's invested in art gallery having three leaflets

indicators.note: something invested in another is placed inside it, like money put into a business

parts.note: the Tate is a famous group of art galleries in Britain
Ernie Wise, Eric Morecambe's partner, was teasingly called 'little Ern'; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Continuing from 4, the duo's smaller partner has put money into a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'their' over from 4-down's Morecambe and Wise; Eric's habit of calling Ernie 'little Ern' was a running joke of their show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ternate is a botanical term for a compound leaf divided into three leaflets, like clover.

clue.text: Ring for sporting combat, Tyson's oddly missing — work hard at the start

indicators.note: at the start means the work and hard pieces come before the rest

parts.note: to do is to work, as in 'do a job'
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: oddly missing means the letters in odd positions are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A boxing ring without Mike Tyson, where you must graft hard from the opening bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyson suggests a boxing ring, but the sport is sumo; the even letters of 'Tyson' give YO.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised clay ring in which sumo wrestlers fight is called by this Japanese word.

clue.text: Fake doctor sectioned son unseen

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged
unseen means the letters of the word son are not used in the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A bogus doctor had a patient sectioned without seeing the patient's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of SON out of SECTIONED to leave ECTIED, which 'doctor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A fake, as a noun, is a deception or sham, the act of misleading by trickery.

clue.text: Norwegian artist detailed Smurf's essence during a spring festival for little people; …

indicators.note: during means within, so these letters go inside the festival

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu festival of colours held in spring

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, losing the last letter

parts.note: Edvard Munch was the Norwegian painter of The Scream

indicators.note: essence means the central heart of the word, its middle letter

explanation.surface: A Norwegian painter puts tiny blue Smurfs into a festival scene of little people.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to 8-down, which tells where the painter died. 'Detailed' looks like 'finely drawn' but means 'tail removed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homunculi are tiny humans or manikins, the Latin plural of the word for a little man.

clue.text: … he died here, content to leave oils, see

indicators.note: content to leave means the inside letters of the word oils depart, keeping only its ends

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Continuing 7, the painter died happy to give up oil painting, look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the Norwegian artist Munch from 7-down; 'content' looks like 'happy' but means the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Munch died in 1944 at his home near the Norwegian capital, so the city is where he died.

clue.text: Prince not quite competing with King after support for filibuster, once

indicators.note: after means the king piece goes behind the support piece rather than before it
not quite means the final letter is left off

parts.note: rival can be used to mean competing, as in rival firms
a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A prince nearly competing with a king, after backing a long-winded speaker in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Filibuster is not the debating tactic but its old sense of a freebooting pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibuster was once a buccaneer, and a privateer was a privately owned ship or sailor licensed to raid enemy shipping.

clue.text: Buff accountant meets half of 1A; …

parts.note: CA is short for chartered accountant
Mel Giedroyc is half of the comedy duo Mel and Sue

explanation.surface: An enthusiast who is an accountant meets one of a comedy pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' looks like an enthusiast, but it is the colour. Mel and Sue are a British comic duo known for presenting The Great British Bake Off.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour, the same shade as the coat of the desert beast of burden.

clue.text: … their partner joins a posh school — discount to follow

indicators.note: to discount is to leave out of account, so the word to is removed

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school, a byword for poshness
Sue Perkins is Mel's partner in the duo Mel and Sue, carried over from 10

explanation.surface: Continuing 10, Mel's partner joins an expensive school and a reduction follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'their' over from 10-across's Mel, so the partner is Sue.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a result is to follow on, the way consequences come after an action.

clue.text: Triumph over former partner in the last month

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ult, short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Getting the better of an ex in the past month.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice in success, to crow over a victory, which is the verb sense of triumph.

clue.text: Idiot disheartened by stage name, touring new Romeo and Juliet, maybe

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letters, are taken out, leaving the outer ones
touring means going round, so the stage name wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a stage name is an alias

explanation.surface: A foolish actor takes a stage name while touring a new production of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet looks like the play but stands for its two characters, both from Verona; 'maybe' marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet are Veronese, so they are examples of people from that Mediterranean country.

clue.text: Supreme German and European achievement knocking the stuffing out of England

parts.note: und is the German word for and
a feat is an achievement

indicators.note: knocking the stuffing out of means the inner letters are removed, leaving the outer ones

explanation.surface: A football report: Germany and another European side triumph, thrashing England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German and' does not mean a German side; it asks for the German word for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion who is never beaten is supreme, unbeaten by any rival in the field.

clue.text: Brown cow's first to bolt — almost a sign of stupidity

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word cow's
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to bolt is to run off, to escape

explanation.surface: A brown cow is first to break out, which was almost a stupid thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall paper cone was once put on a slow pupil's head as a badge of dimness in class.

clue.text: Comfortable in retirement, goes shooting …

indicators.note: in retirement means going backwards, retreating, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: snug means comfortable and cosy

explanation.surface: A cosy retiree takes up shooting, which runs on into 18's fish in a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To gun is to fire a weapon, so this verb form describes someone who goes out firing at targets.

clue.text: Tray not right for cream

indicators.note: not right means the letter R, for right, is removed

parts.note: a salver is a flat serving tray

explanation.surface: A tray left out of place for the cream jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like dairy but is an ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A healing ointment or balm rubbed on the skin is a kind of cream.

clue.text: Make Tom log on again without a second language

indicators.note: make together with again asks for the letters to be made over in a new order
again, with make, signals the letters are remade into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Tom has to log in once more, and can only manage in one language.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who speaks only one tongue is monolingual, lacking any second language.

clue.text: … fish in a barrel to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means the barrel piece comes first, before the a

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: Continuing 15, shooting fish in a barrel, the proverbial easy task.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface completes the idiom 'like shooting fish in a barrel'; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuna is a large sea fish, often sold canned.

clue.text: Unfriendly half of 1A's old agents left; …

parts.note: Ant McPartlin is half of the TV duo Ant and Dec; the 's is read as is
the CIA is the US intelligence agency, staffed by agents

explanation.surface: One half of a comedy pair is unfriendly, and his old spy contacts have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting duo; read the 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfriendly avoids the company of others and is unsociable, hostile to mixing.

clue.text: Secure lock for salon

parts.note: to nail is to secure, fasten down
to bar a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: Fit a secure lock on a beauty salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop where manicures are done is a kind of beauty salon.

clue.text: I belong for a change — that's mean

indicators.note: for a change says the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who for once feels they fit in, and finds it petty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of base or dishonourable, lacking noble qualities, low and contemptible.

clue.text: Shame to embrace the extremes of godliness for a place far from cleanliness

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so these letters sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a shame, as in 'what a shame', is a pity

indicators.note: the extremes of means the outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A play on the proverb 'cleanliness is next to godliness'.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says cleanliness is next to godliness, so a filthy place is far from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A filthy pen where pigs live is the byword for a squalid, dirty place.

clue.text: … their partner is working on current recommendation

indicators.note: on means placed after, so working follows current

parts.note: Declan Donnelly is Ant's partner in Ant and Dec, carried over from 19
I is the symbol for electric current
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Continuing 19, Ant's partner is working on current advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'their' over from 19-across's Ant, so the partner is Dec.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling or judgment that is reached, such as a panel's verdict, amounts to a recommendation.

clue.text: Sheepish individual seen around six

indicators.note: around means the individual piece wraps about the other

parts.note: one means a single individual
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A shy person seen at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like embarrassed but is taken literally: relating to sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means of or like sheep, a literal reading of sheepish.

clue.text: More hostile French here before the Queen

parts.note: ici is French for here
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: The French are less friendly here in front of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A colder, frostier manner is more hostile, as in an icy stare.

clue.text: Backing singer's enthusiastic

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A backing singer is keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing singer' reads as one phrase, but 'backing' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and keen, as an avid reader is.

clue.text: Bad habits formed when half of 1A succeeded taking drug; …

indicators.note: taking means holding in, so the drug goes inside

parts.note: Vic Reeves is half of the comedy duo Vic and Bob
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
E is the slang abbreviation for ecstasy

explanation.surface: One half of a comedy act got into bad habits by taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Vic Reeves and Bob Mortimer are a surreal British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad habits are faults or failings, moral weaknesses like smoking or drinking.

clue.text: … their partner starts to swear like most of 8 and it goes downhill fast

parts.note: Bob Mortimer is Vic's partner, carried over from 27

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letters of the following words
most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: the figure 8 is written as a word here

explanation.surface: Continuing 27, Bob begins to curse at an eight, and it all goes downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a reference to 8-down but is just the number eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing sled for winter sport runs at speed down an icy track.

clue.text: Experienced laughter on 1A's introduction

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: ha is the sound of laughter

indicators.note: introduction means the first letter of the word, its opening

parts.note: 1A is the across answer clued as an entertaining pair, the puzzle's theme

explanation.surface: Laughter greets the entertaining pair's opening act.
explanation.definitionFit: To have experienced something is to have undergone it, as in 'went through a rough time'.

clue.text: Gen Y appear to be stupid

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as is dope, the inside story

explanation.surface: Members of Generation Y seem foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gen Y' looks like the generation, but 'Gen' is slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means dim-witted or slow, like the dwarf of that name.

clue.text: Two Ronnies — both on vacation — entertaining awkward teen before director came back in

indicators.note: before means the earlier part comes first and director goes last
entertaining means having as a guest inside, so one piece goes within
two means two copies of the emptied name are used
on vacation means emptied, so the inner letters of each name leave

parts.note: Ronnie, as in Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett, the double act The Two Ronnies

indicators.note: awkward says the letters are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: The Two Ronnies host an awkward teenager before a film director returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges TEEN as ENTE, which sits between RE and RE. The Two Ronnies were a hugely popular British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come back into a place, so this past form means came back in.
